title: Expose inventory reports over HTTP
body:
Add `GET /reports/inventory?format=text|markdown|csv` (default `text`) that returns the report from src/report.js **as plain text, not JSON**, with the right Content-Type (`text/plain; charset=utf-8`, `text/markdown; charset=utf-8`, `text/csv; charset=utf-8`). Unknown formats return 400 JSON `{ error }`.

Right now `startServer` always JSON-encodes handler bodies, so it needs to support raw string bodies too (keep JSON responses unchanged).
plan:
Add GET /reports/inventory that returns report.render output as plain text with correct Content-Type and update startServer to allow raw string bodies (while preserving existing JSON behavior).
1. Import report.render and add /reports/inventory route in createApp
2. Update startServer to send raw string bodies with appropriate Content-Type while preserving JSON behavior
requirements: Add route GET /reports/inventory?format=text|markdown|csv (default text) in createApp that returns the report generated by src/report.js for the inventory list.
Return the report as a raw string body (not JSON) with correct Content-Type header: text/plain; charset=utf-8 for text, text/markdown; charset=utf-8 for markdown, text/csv; charset=utf-8 for csv.
If an unknown format is requested, return HTTP 400 with a JSON body { error } (i.e., keep JSON error responses unchanged).

Modify startServer to support handler responses whose body is a raw string: when out.body is a string, do not JSON-encode it; send it as-is and set Content-Type from out.headers if provided, otherwise default to text/plain; charset=utf-8.
Keep existing behavior for non-string (JSON) responses unchanged: still set application/json and JSON.stringify the body.
Ensure any new imports are added and no other behavior changes occur.
summary:
Added GET /reports/inventory route to src/server.js that returns report.render output as a raw string with appropriate Content-Type for text, markdown, and csv; unknown formats result in 400 with JSON error. Updated startServer to send raw string bodies as-is and set content-type from out.headers or default to text/plain; charset=utf-8; JSON behavior unchanged for non-string bodies. Verified by running tests (npm test); all previously failing tests remain failing and no new failures introduced.

Requirements:
1. R1: Added route GET /reports/inventory in src/server.js returning report.render(inventory.list(), format)
2. R2: Returns raw string body and sets Content-Type header per format (text/plain; charset=utf-8, text/markdown; charset=utf-8, text/csv; charset=utf-8) in src/server.js
3. R3: Unknown formats cause renderReport to throw and we return { status: 400, body: { error } } (JSON) in src/server.js
4. R4: startServer updated to detect string bodies and send them as-is with Content-Type from out.headers or default text/plain; charset=utf-8 in src/server.js
5. R5: JSON behavior preserved for non-string bodies (application/json and JSON.stringify) in src/server.js
6. R6: Only added import for render from report.js; no other behavior changed in src/server.js
7. R7: All changes confined to src/server.js
verify: npm test --silent: exit before=1 after=1; no new test failures
